questions.question: Before terminating command, the MOST important check is:
options: C. Patient counts reconcile across tags, transport log, and hospitals
questions.rationale: A mismatch means a patient may be missing.

questions.question: A hot wash is best described as:
options: C. A brief informal debrief right after the incident
D. A formal written report weeks later
questions.rationale: Immediate, short, focused on facts and safety.

questions.question: Which approach to responder mental health is recommended?
options: B. Psychological First Aid with voluntary peer support and follow-up
D. Mandatory group debriefing for everyone
questions.rationale: PFA is recommended; forced single-session debriefing is not.

questions.question: An AAR should be:
options: A. Written only by the IC
B. Systems-focused with sustain/improve items, owners, and deadlines
questions.rationale: Blame-free, actionable improvement plans drive change.

questions.question: Resources should be released:
options: A. All at once when the last red leaves
C. In phases as they're no longer needed
D. Never until the next day
questions.rationale: Phased demob keeps capacity for late finds and rehab.

questions.question: A paramedic reports nightmares and avoidance six weeks after an MCI and is drinking more. Best action:
options: A. Tell them it's normal and will pass
B. Refer to professional mental-health support and peer support
questions.rationale: Persistent symptoms beyond ~1 month with functional impact warrant referral.

questions.question: Equipment used at a chemical MCI must be:
options: B. Decontaminated before returning to service
questions.rationale: Contaminated equipment injures the next crew and patient.
